sections.heading: What is Clutter ? Why is it difficult to get rid of it ?

headings.text: What is Clutter ? Why is it difficult to get rid of it ?

paragraphs: By Sevadeep | Aug 4, 2022 | Others

Anything and everything that we buy but don't use & is lying around somewhere in our home is what we call Clutter. 

How is clutter formed:- 

With the advancement of advertising & social media, Bollywood divas & superheroes endorsing clothing to cosmetics, perfumes to consumer durables, you name it and it is there in the media. These days we have influencers endorsing products too, and it becomes almost impossible to not fall for it. 

We buy things that are NOT necessarily needed just because we feel the need to satiate our thirst for being updated, well dressed, presentable, and confident every day. 

Sometimes it is ok to buy the stuff you like, but for many, it becomes a habit which eventually leads to the birth of a special category of people called "Shopaholics''. To make matters worse, every now & then there are e-commerce websites sprouting up with humongous discounts and lucrative deals you just cannot ignore which adds fuel to the fire.

People do comfort shopping just to feel good when they are depressed or feeling down thinking retail therapy can help them, which in turn leads to debts, despair & piling up of unwanted things.

​Why is it difficult to get rid of it?

1) Emotional attachment - The things we might have used on any special occasion like wedding, 1st birthday, bought from 1st salary, a gift from someone special, etc gives sentimental value to it and becomes really hard to give away.

2) We might need it one day - We keep thinking that someday we might need it and then we don't have to buy new. So, it is kind of an investment for the future which never disburses.

3) It is comforting - Many people find it comforting to keep things piled up as they use it as a cushion for the emotional or physical turmoil they go through. 

4) Guilt - There is a feeling of guilt for having spent money and not using it, hence we hold on to it.

What is the solution ??

Donate - Many things are in good condition but are of no use to us, which can be useful to someone. Why not bring a smile on the face of that someone by giving? Not only are you removing clutter from your home, but you are also helping some needy too. Adding Good Karma for yourself is a bonus. Seems to be a good deal…isn’t it?

www.sevadeep.org is one of the digital platforms that connects donors with NGOs across India. You can easily register your donation and rest assured your donation will reach a genuine & needy NGO from your city.

Upcycle - As time passes, there are clothes we don’t fit into or electronic items which are not working but are in a good condition. These can be fitted/altered/repaired and reused. That way you bring them into use and you don’t have to buy new ones. A penny saved is a penny earned… What say ??

Recycle - There are things that are completely worn out and are of no use, all those can be sent to scrap dealers or kabadiwala. Following waste management organizations may help:-

https://www.attero.in/ 

https://www.banyannation.com/ 

https://craste.co/ 

http://www.lucro.in/ 

https://phool.co/ 

Decluttering not only helps clean our home, but it also creates a positive atmosphere, as they say, cluttered home, cluttered life. When we see our home clean and organized, we see a significant decrease in the stress hormone helping us feel more stable, clear-headed, and relaxed.

sections.heading: It’s Time To Donate a Merry Christmas!

headings.text: It’s Time To Donate a Merry Christmas!

paragraphs: By SevaDeep | Dec 8, 2020 | Original

Nothing resonates more with Christmas than the spirit of giving and sharing. It is the time of the year when we should all share a little with those who have less and are not as fortunate as some are.




In spirit of the holiday, we created a list of the most popular items you can donate this Christmas, to make it a genuinely happy and memorable one for hundreds of people!

1.      Donate your old books:

The Christmas season brings with it cold weather that could have everyone tucked in their warm homes. To help those in need pass the time, donate your old books to SevaDeep so we may distribute them amongst the NGOs that are listed on our platform.

2.      Donate warm clothes and blankets:

While we are on the subject of cold weather, look deep in your closet and pull out the warm items that you no longer want or need. If you have children that have outgrown their clothes, this is the perfect opportunity to do some winter cleaning and donate your old clothes to SevaDeep, so we may distribute them to hundreds of children that need to stay warm during these cold winter months.

3.      Sponsor a meal:

SevaDeep’s mission of sponsoring grocery kits for those in need began in the early days of the COVID lockdown. In this period, we have reached out to hundreds of people (patients and relatives) and supported them with warm meals.

Now that the lockdown is over, our team has the ability to travel to more remote areas and support those in need. To know more about the sponsor a meal program, click here.

4.      Donate old furniture:

The winter furniture sales are the perfect opportunity to finally change the old beds and couches. Donate your old furniture items to SevaDeep so we may deliver them to old age homes and orphanages around the city. You don’t have to worry about transportation. Our team will be happy to pick your old items from your doorstep.

5.      Donate old appliances:

Bought a new TV or a fridge? Send the old appliances our way and we will deliver them to those who need them the most! Just remember to make sure that they are in a working condition so others may enjoy them.

During the holiday season, our team gears up with extra helping hands to make sure we can address the increased number of donations efficiently. Help us make sure our team works hard all the way to the end of the year!

Be sure to check out specific NGO requirements here. Follow us on Facebook for more news and updates.

sections.heading: Join the SevaDeep Sponsor a Meal Program

headings.text: Join the SevaDeep Sponsor a Meal Program

paragraphs: By SevaDeep | Nov 19, 2020 | Original

194 million Indians are undernourished, and our country is ranked 94th out of 107 countries in the Global Hunger Index, a measurement of the world’s hunger and malnutrition levels. According to the GHI report, 14 per cent of India’s population is undernourished. It also says that the country recorded a child stunting rate of 37.4 per cent.

The country lockdown during spread of the COVID pandemic made food sourcing even more difficult for thousands of people. It caused a food shortage across the nation, disrupting local, regional, and national food supply chains.

As a quick response to this urgent matter, SevaDeep launched Narayan Seva, a specialized, dedicated food service that provides free meals to the underprivileged masses. Narayan Seva, our long-distance food delivery program, delivers food to those in need, especially in distant regions, labor camps and chall areas.

“We made sure we make food accessible to everyone in need during these tough times. The food is cooked in the SevaDeep kitchen and we follow all the safety measures outlined by the authorities.”, says Nitin, SevaDeep’s Head of Operations.

The Sponsor a Meal Program would not be possible without the support of hundreds of people who opened their hearts and donated to the cause. A simple donation of Rs. 3,000 helps us feed 200 people. Thousands have already benefited from the program and its popularity is only growing. Reports of food shortages land in our system on a daily basis and we can only cope with the requirements with your support.

In case you’d like to know more about the program, or you are interested in making a donation, visit the Sponsor a Meal Program page on our website. 

Remember that there are hundreds of other NGOs that could use your support in other forms. The NGO near you could benefit from your donation of old clothes, furniture, appliances, toys or books. Check out our list of NGO requirements here.

Thanks to your support, we have onboarded over 420 NGOs till date and have completed over 1,500 donations. Spread the word and help us bridge the gap between more donors and NGOs.

Be sure to follow us on Facebook for more news and updates on our work.

sections.heading: Five Ways To Make Diwali Really Special

headings.text: Five Ways To Make Diwali Really Special

paragraphs: By SevaDeep | Nov 10, 2020 | Original

Our favorite festival is right around the corner and we must say, after this year’s COVID rollercoaster, it couldn’t come at a better time!

For many of us, this is the time to give. Buildings are collecting a “Deepavali funds"




for the staff;companies are handing out bonuses and charities around the country are gearing up for donations.

The festivities bring people together; they celebrate new beginnings and share their happiness. For the kind at heart, the festival is marked by reaching out to the less fortunate and donating to charity. Today, we’d like to bring to you five ways in which you can make Diwali really special this year.

Replace your children’s old toys with new ones and donate your old ones to Shree Santraj Yogi Shikshan Sanstha. The Pune based NGO operates an orphanage and addresses all the needs of children that lost their families.
Cook the grandest meal ever but add a few more items to donate to the Maya Care Centre. The Maya Care Centre is an old age home that has been serving the elderly for the last 7 years. The foundation has 25 beneficiaries and is located in Pune. They need Wheat, Rice, Peanuts, Oil and Masale. For more information, click here
Buy new clothes for family members and donate your old ones to Dnyanjyoti Bahuuddeshiya Sanstha. This foundation works round the clock to ensure the underprivileged have good clothes to wear. Their work benefits hundreds of people from the ages of 10 to 65+.
Bring home new warm winter blankets and send your old ones to Vidya Edu IX Foundation. The organisation is still working round the clock to help families in the Wambhori village, who were affected by heavy floods earlier this year. For more information, click here.  
Did you decide to gift yourself a new dining set? Shree Santraj Yogi Shikshan Sanstha could really use your old one! The foundation is in urgent need of plates and spoons to feed the underprivileged families it supports on a daily basis.

There are hundreds of other NGOs and Foundations near you that could benefit from your donations and guess what, they are all on the SevaDeep platform!

Visit us today to make a donation to the NGO near you and put a smile on the faces of those who are less fortunate.

Don’t forget to stay in touch with SevaDeep’s activities on Facebook.

sections.heading: SevaDeep Monthly NGO Review | October 2020 | Support The NGO Near You

headings.text: SevaDeep Monthly NGO Review | October 2020 | Support The NGO Near You

paragraphs: By SevaDeep | Oct 22, 2020 | Original

The monsoons are almost over and we’d like to thank each and every one of the donors who made the season more comfortable for those in need. Thanks to your donations and support, children in orphanages and the elderly in the old age homes we support were able to keep warm and stay healthy. 

During the month of October, we onboarded two new NGOs and completed a total of 79 deliveries of clothes, medicines, furniture, toys, books and food items. The donations were carried out across the state in Pune, Nashik, Mumbai and Aurangabad. 

Today, we would like to bring to your attention a few new foundations on the SevaDeep platform that may benefit from your donations. If you are in a position to donate the required items to any of these NGOs, simply click the relevant links and complete the donation form. 

As always, our team will be more than happy to pick up the items from your doorstep and deliver them safely to the NGO. 

Snehalaya Institute for Handicapped:

1.The Thane based NGO supports handicapped children and young adults. The foundation makes a wide range of skill programs accessible to mentally and physically challenged individuals, in an effort to create opportunities for them. sections.heading: How I Donated to the NGO Near Me

headings.text: How I Donated to the NGO Near Me

paragraphs: By Maria J | Oct 5, 2020 | Original

While packing for relocation, I discovered a huge pile of items that were no longer needed. Clothes, old toys the kids used to play with, board games, puzzles and a few furniture items like chairs and a work desk. 




I tried my best to find some use to al these items but honestly, with all the hassle of packing and leaving the apartment I was in, giving them away seemed to be the best option. 

I thought about the underprivileged children living in foundation homes around the city and quickly realised that giving all my old clothing items, toys and furniture to them would be a much better option than just throwing them away. 

The next task in front of me was locating a good NGO near me, that provided enough information on how my old items can be used and where they are headed. I was determined to make sure my old items won’t end up in the dump yard. 

A quick google search led me to SevaDeep, an initiative by Pune’s Relfor Foundation, that bridges the gap between donors and NGOs. The digital platform lists thousands of NGOs around the country, their contact details, their area of work and the current requirements. I was happy to see that the platform only accepted donations of old appliances, furniture, clothes, toys, without engaging in monetary donations. The platform also authenticates each and every NGO. 

After scrolling through for a few minutes, I came across Shree Santraj Yogi Shikshan Sanstha. According to the SevaDeep platform, the foundation provides a safe home for children of single parents, who cannot support themselves. This looked like a good match for me. I clicked the donate button and after filling a few details, I received a confirmation and a scheduled time for pick up of my donation (this was an extremely pleasant surprise). 

The SevaDeep truck arrived a few minutes before the scheduled time, and the driver examined my items. After verifying that they were indeed usable, he packed them on the truck and informed me that he was going to the item storage and that within a day or two, all my items will be delivered to the NGO. 

The entire experience was absolutely flawless. The entire process, from the decision to donate the items to their pickup by the SevaDeep team, didn’t take more than a couple of hours, and I had no hassles. 

The kind SevaDeep representative just asked me to sign my pickup note and refused to accept the tip I offered.

It’s been a couple of months since I made my first donation to the NGO near me through SevaDeep. Although I have settled in my new apartment, I can tell you that I constantly look for items to donate to the NGOs that they list on the platform. 

The initiative is the need of the hour, especially now that these wonderful volunteers, the foundations and the people they serve face acute shortages due to the lockdown and tough weather. 

I urge you all to visit their website and schedule a donation of your old items today! Don’t forget to follow them on Facebook for more news. A big shout out to their team for the great service and initiative.

headings.text: SevaDeep Monthly NGO Review | September 2020 | Current NGO Needs in Pune City

paragraphs: By SevaDeep | Sep 25, 2020 | Donations

As we approach the end of September, we’d like to summarise our activity and share updates from our work with the numerous NGO’s and Foundations of the country.

During the month of September, we

registered a large number of new NGOs. Today, there are 423 organisations listed on the SevaDeep platform and they could all use your help!

We also recorded over one thousand donations till date since the launch of our initiate and addressed the needs of over three hundred foundations.

These numbers are impressive albeit we cannot forget the thousands of people who could still benefit from your donation of old items, old clothes, toys, furniture, old electrical appliances and dry food items.

Today, we would like to introduce three organisations that could use your help.

1.     Shree Santraj Yogi Shikshan Sanstha

The foundation is based in Galandwadi, Pune and is home to many orphans and single parents. The NGO provides a safe home to displaced individuals and children and supports them by providing them education, food, shelter and engaging in extra curricular activities. The NGO has an urgent requirement of clothes, utensils, legumes and toys or games. If you have old items to donate and would like to make a donation to this foundation, click here.

2.     Yashottam Janhit Pratishthan

This foundation is based in Hadapsar, Pune and provides a safe and nurturing environment to young children. The NGO structures a wide array of social and educational programs, environmental awareness and sanitation programs and a safe haven for children in need. The foundation is in urgent need of educational supplies for a new school they constructed in a nearby village. For more information, click here.

3.      Caring Hands Old Age Home

The foundation is operated by Madhunand Society and currently houses 100 individuals above the age of 65. These displaced individuals have lost their family and the NGO provides them a safe roof over their head. The organisation is in need of three bookshelves for its new library. If you have shelves you can donate, click here.

Be sure to stay tuned to the latest happenings on our Facebook page. Check out the other NGO requirements directly on the platform.

Remember, every blessed human being has a kind side and wants to help the less fortunate ones. SevaDeep is here to help you reach those in need.

sections.heading: Supporting Old Age Homes
paragraphs: By SevaDeep | Sep 18, 2020 | Donations

Elderly homes around the country support a large number of senior citizens that are in need of assisted living or a roof over their heads. The population of that belongs to this age group has increased steadily since the 1950s. The Census of India 2001 enumerated approximately 7.6 crore senior citizens in India, which has increased to 10.4 crores in 2011.

With the rising income levels, a growing number of these senior citizens are now economically independent and willing to pay for senior living facilities and services related to their physical, medical and psychological needs. However, an extremely large number of elderly people lack the economic means or support from their families and have no choice but to move to special homes for the senior or shelter homes that can provide them with a comfortable elderly living environment, meals or medical care.

There are numerous foundations on the SevaDeep platform that provide care services to elderly parents who have no home or family. There are approximately 728 old age shelters in India today. 101 of these are reserved for women and 278 old age homes support aged parents with medical needs.

These facilities need everyone’s support to operate. Close to 18 million people above the age of 60 in India are homeless and these old age homes provide them love, respect and dignity in the late stages of their lives.

What can you donate?




1. Old furniture

Old age homes are constantly in need of cupboards, sofa sets, chairs, tables and beds.




2. Blankets, throws or shawls

According to agingcare.com, seniors can become “dangerously chilled because they have less fat, slower circulation, and more sluggish metabolism. A senior can even become hypothermic while indoors.” Receiving a blanket or shawl can warm the body and the heart.




3. Old appliances

Old TV sets, microwaves and refrigerators are crucial appliances for many old age homes.




4. Games, puzzles and books

Nothing keeps the mind active and can provide hours of fun like games and books. If you’d like to give away some of these items, old age homes will be happy to take them.




Log on to the SevaDeep platform and browse through our list of senior citizen homes to view their needs. If you have items to donate, just schedule your donation on the platform and we will take care of the rest. Stay tuned for more news and updates from SevaDeep on our Facebook page .

sections.heading: What Are The Best Things To Donate To An Orphanage?

headings.text: What Are The Best Things To Donate To An Orphanage?

paragraphs: By SevaDeep | Sep 15, 2020 | Childcare & Education

Children residing in Child Care Institutions (CCIs, or orphanages) in India often lag behind when it comes to support and development initiatives. The COVID-19 lockdown made the situation worse, with the number of donations to such institutions freezing completely. There are about 370,000 children in more than 9,500 CCIs in India. Each and every child in these centres could benefit from a simple donation you can make through the SevaDeep platform. 

Growing children need clothes, which makes them one of the best items to donate to children living in orphanages. Children in orphanages are usually between the ages of 3 and 18 so remember to keep that in mind when choosing which clothing items to donate. 

School supplies are also extremely important for children in orphanages. These foundations often take care of the children’s education and supporting them with stationary will help their cause. 

Another important donation item for children is toys! Nothing brings a bigger smile to a child’s face than toys and we can see them playing enthusiastically at every orphanage we visit. If you have old toys you can donate, click here! 

This month, we would like to bring to your attention two exceptional foundations that support young children. 

1. Toybrary from Ahmed Nagar works round the clock to take care of children in rural areas 

and support their education and development. Toybrary came to life by Donate Aid Society, Pune, especially for Anganwadi children. To develop their motor and cognitive skills along with hand-eye co-ordination and mainly encouraging them to come to school. If you’d like to make a donation to Toybrary, click here! 

﻿2. Disha Kendra from Mulshi is an organisation that uplifts socio-economically weaker tribal communities. The organization provides basic infrastructure and facilities to those in need and supports the education and development of young children. If you’d like to make a donation to Disha Kendra, click here! 

Children are the future of our nation and empowering them is investing in the country’s development. Support the orphanages that provide safe homes for these children today! 

SevaDeep has helped hundreds of NGOs and thousands of people in need to date. Don’t forget to follow SevaDeep on Facebook and spread the word of our work to your local community!

sections.heading: Want to Donate to Individuals? SevaDeep is here for you!

headings.text: Want to Donate to Individuals? SevaDeep is here for you!

paragraphs: By ADMIN | Aug 27, 2020 | Donations

We are constantly working to improve our platform and make donations more accessible to those who need them the most. Over the last year, we have focused on addressing the needs of NGOs, foundations and organisations that extend a helping hand to the segments of society that need help the most. Today, we are proud to announce that you can now donate to individuals!

The efficiency of the SevaDeep platform has proven itself by bringing NGOs and Donors closer together. We have registered over 400 NGOs and completed over 800 donations. The donors on the platform have donated items ranging from toys and clothes to furniture and helped thousands of people in need.

During the Nisarg Cyclone that hit Mumbai, we managed to provide relief in the form of grocery kits, solar lamps, roof covers and clothes. The COVID 19 lockdown that left thousands of people stranded also proved to be a challenging period. Our donation kits supported hundreds of stranded individuals in Maharashtra and helped uphold the unorganized labour sector.

As a result of these events, we realised that many individuals cannot access the framework of an NGO or a foundation. This encouraged us to launch the Individual Donations Platform on SevaDeep. Under this segment of the platform, you may view the needs of individuals in different cities. You may also search for individual requirements by categories. When you schedule a donation, our team will visit you to collect your donation and deliver it safely to the concerned individual.

We are working round the clock to create an ecosystem of giving, in a way that bridges the gap between needs and fulfilment. Remember to look for the “NGO near me” on the SeveDeep platform and schedule your donation today.

Be sure to follow us on Facebook for more news and updates.
